finding.claim: DELETE /reports/:id deletes any report regardless of the caller's grants because authorize() is called without await, so its 403 rejection is discarded and the delete proceeds.
finding.source: Any request to DELETE /reports/:id by a session user (req.user from req.session.user, server.js:5) who lacks a 'delete' grant on the target report.

trace.note: req.user = req.session.user; no check that the user is authenticated or that the session exists
report loaded by attacker-supplied req.params.id with no ownership or grant pre-filter
authorize(req.user,'delete',report) is NOT awaited; it returns a Promise, so the throw of err.status=403 at :14 becomes a rejected Promise nobody handles and execution continues

finding.guards_checked: authorize() at server.js:9-16 correctly computes and throws 403 but its result never gates the delete. Express 4 would not catch the async rejection either. No route-level middleware, no unhandledRejection handler and no await-based guard are present in this file. Session middleware that sets req.session is not in this file and was not verified.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. authorize() at server.js:9-16 throws a 403 on missing grant, but line 20 calls it without await, so the returned rejected promise is never tested and execution continues to db.reports.remove at server.js:21. No route-level middleware, unhandledRejection handler, or await-based guard exists in server.js. The session middleware that populates req.session (cited at server.js:5) is not in this file and was not verified; it only gates whether the attacker needs a session, not whether the grant check runs.
verdict.reason: The grant check at server.js:20 is a bare, un-awaited call whose 403 rejection is discarded, so the unconditional db.reports.remove at server.js:21 runs for any session user lacking a 'delete' grant, and the 204 at server.js:22 confirms success. The attacker only needs an authenticated low-privilege session, which is a real authorization bypass. A caveat that does not refute it: on Node 15+ the unhandled rejection can crash the process once db.grants resolves, but the remove I/O is already in flight by then.

finding.claim: Unauthorized or malformed requests to PUT /reports/:id produce a rejected async handler that Express 4 does not catch. This leaves the request hanging and, on Node 15+ without an unhandledRejection handler, can crash the process (remote DoS by any session user or unauthenticated request).
finding.source: Any PUT /reports/:id where the caller lacks a 'write' grant (throws 403 at :14), the report id does not exist (report is null at :26), or req.user is undefined because there is no session user (user.id at :10 throws TypeError).
finding.sink: Unhandled promise rejection from the async route handler at server.js:25-30; process termination under default Node behavior.

trace.note: req.user is undefined when req.session.user is unset
db.reports.get returns null for a nonexistent id
await authorize(...) rejects with 403 or TypeError (resource.id on null / user.id on undefined)
db.grants(user.id, resource.id) throws TypeError when user or resource is missing
async handler with no try/catch and no next(err); Express 4 does not forward promise rejections

finding.guards_checked: The await at :27 does propagate the rejection, which is correct for the 403 path, but Express 4 ignores it. There is no try/catch, no error middleware in this file and no process-level unhandledRejection handler. The Express version is not pinned in this directory, so the crash behavior depends on the installed version. Confidence is medium.

verdict.guard_found: none in server.js. No try/catch around the PUT handler (server.js:25-30), no error-handling middleware, and no process-level unhandledRejection handler. The authorize() call at :27 is awaited, so its 403 or TypeError does reject the handler's promise.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code at server.js:5, 10, 26, 27 and 25, and an authenticated low-privilege user can reach the unguarded rejection at :27. Whether the process crashes or the request hangs depends on the Express version, which is not pinned here (no package.json found in the directory). Express 4 does not forward async rejections, but Express 5 does, so the claim cannot be confirmed from the code available. Also, server.js:5 reads req.session.user, and the session middleware that sets req.session is not in this file.

finding.claim: PUT /reports/:id passes the entire unfiltered req.body to db.reports.update, enabling mass assignment. A user holding only a 'write' grant can overwrite any stored report field, such as owner, ACL, or identifier fields, if the schema contains them.
finding.source: req.body, parsed from attacker-controlled JSON at server.js:3, by any caller holding a 'write' grant on the report (server.js:27 check).

trace.note: express.json() parses arbitrary JSON bodies, with no field allowlist
authorize 'write' on that report; succeeds for a writer
entire req.body is written to the record; fields like owner_id, id or grant-related fields are not excluded

finding.guards_checked: Authorization is checked at :27 for the target record. No field allowlist, schema validation or stripping of protected fields exists in this file. The db.reports schema is not in the repo, so the real impact depends on which fields are stored. Confidence is medium and depends on the schema.

verdict.guard_found: The write check at server.js:27 (`await authorize(req.user, "write", report)`) is awaited and throws a 403 on failure, so it gates the route but does not filter fields. No field allowlist or protected-field stripping exists in server.js. The only other control is `db.reports.update` at server.js:28, whose implementation is not in the repo and could filter fields.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches server.js (express.json at :3, load at :26, awaited write check at :27, unfiltered `db.reports.update(report.id, req.body)` at :28), and a writer can reach it, but whether it is exploitable depends on fields in the db.reports schema and on whether db.reports.update filters fields, and neither is in the repo.
